title: Preserve scheduler phase after delayed wakes
environment: Recorded synthetic consumer path. The numbers do not prove later wrapper or live cadence, and skipping ticks is inappropriate for workloads requiring every event.
goal: Consume the latest sample near a configured periodic rate.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Processing duration and repeated wake delay were assumed not to accumulate into schedule drift.
what_worked: Historical correction: Preserve the original deadline phase, include work within each period, skip missed ticks without catch-up replay, and consume newest state only. Verification reported by the source: Deterministic work/early-wake/late-wake/burst/stall controls passed. Repeated synthetic IPC measurements improved approximately 21.635 to 30.143 Hz and 32.316 to 58.876 Hz.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: Sleeping a full period after work delivered about 21.6 Hz at a 30 Hz target and 32.3 Hz at 60 Hz. Resetting deadlines from each late start also failed.
why: Confirmed: work-plus-sleep and late-start phase resets continually moved the deadline grid.
improved_method: Test processing time and delayed wakes explicitly. Preserve phase for periodic latest-state work and report measured cadence rather than claiming the configured rate.
when_to_use: Recorded synthetic consumer path. The numbers do not prove later wrapper or live cadence, and skipping ticks is inappropriate for workloads requiring every event.
when_not_to_use: The numbers do not prove later wrapper or live cadence, and skipping ticks is inappropriate for workloads requiring every event.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
